stem: When arterial blood pressure rises, baroreceptor firing rate most likely does which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreases because stretch receptors are inhibited by higher pressure
options.explanation: Baroreceptors increase firing when arterial pressure rises; decreased firing occurs when pressure falls.

options.label: B
options.text: Increases because greater vessel wall stretch activates the receptors
options.misconception: None; increased pressure raises baroreceptor firing rate.
options.explanation: Increased blood pressure stretches carotid and aortic baroreceptors, producing increased rates of baroreceptor firing.

options.label: C
options.text: No change because baroreceptors respond only to oxygen tension
options.misconception: Chemoreceptor function is being substituted for baroreceptor function.
options.explanation: Baroreceptors sense arterial stretch and pressure; chemoreceptors monitor blood gas and pH.

options.label: D
options.text: Complete cessation of firing until pressure normalizes
options.misconception: Baroreceptors are being treated as on–off switches rather than graded sensors.
options.explanation: Baroreceptors fire continuously at a rate proportional to pressure; rising pressure increases, not abolishes, firing.

options.label: E
options.text: Firing only during expiration when intrathoracic pressure rises
options.misconception: A respiratory-cycle artifact is being confused with arterial baroreceptor behavior.
options.explanation: Carotid and aortic baroreceptors track arterial pressure continuously, not only during a respiratory phase.

context: Learning objective: state the baroreceptor firing response to pressure. Increased blood pressure increases baroreceptor firing; decreased pressure slows firing.
